parsed.reason: The facts are accurately reflected (both names and ages, including the "half" detail the parent used). However, the acknowledgment reads like a database readback — it literally recites both name-age pairs in list form rather than sounding like a natural human reply. A warmer, plainer version ("Got it — Priya (5) and Arjun (2½).") would feel less mechanical. It also wastes characters on repetition when the parent gave a fair amount of context (new to the area, swimming lessons frustration) that could have been lightly touched, though it correctly avoids inventing facts. The robotic structure is the main penalty.
